key_insight: PIML-OFEM combines overlapping finite elements with problem-independent machine learning to reuse local basis functions across load cases and boundary conditions for large heterogeneous structures.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster, high-resolution structural analysis and topology optimization while maintaining accuracy close to fine-scale finite element solutions.
method: Each substructure keeps only corner-node degrees of freedom.
Oversampled local basis functions are computed on extended domains and restricted back to the target substructure.
A U-Net predicts basis functions from local Young's modulus fields, and a partition-of-unity overlap ensures global continuity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with fine-scale FEM for displacement and elemental strain energy, with lower online cost than direct FEM and better accuracy than PIML substructure models using linear boundary interpolation.
watch_item: The approach still depends on learning reliable basis mappings from representative material distributions, so performance may degrade for unseen heterogeneity or poorly covered training sets.
paper_title: PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique
